[Feature] Support ModelSlim INT8 and MXFP8 PLE embeddings for Qwen3.8 (#22077)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Enable ModelSlim group-32 INT8 and MXFP8 PLE embeddings for
Qwen3.8-Flash-Next. Quantized PLE tables remain compact on the NPU or in
registered host memory; lookup dequantizes only requested rows to BF16
instead of expanding the full table.

- **Checkpoint loading:** infer the PLE format independently of the
linear/MoE quantization recipe, load INT8 codes with FP32
`shard_N.scale` or E4M3FN codes with E8M0 `shard_N.weight_scale`, and
validate scale coverage and shard mapping.
- **Model integration:** select the quantized embedding method through
the existing ModelSlim PLE adapter. Preserve BF16 behavior, host-buffer
ownership/cleanup, owner-only shared writes and the upstream
TP/sequence-parallel reduction contract.
- **Triton host lookup:** expose `lookup_quantized` in the independent
`ple_lookup_quantized.py` module, validate metadata, gather owned rows
and fuse group-32 dequantization into a caller-provided BF16 output.
Non-owned rows are zeroed before any host gather. Resident lookup uses a
separate PyTorch implementation.
- **Review deliverables:** include the operator contract
(`vllm_ascend/ops/triton/docs/ple_lookup_quantized.md`), CPU/NPU
regression tests, a reproducible operator benchmark and a release note.

This is a model-specific memory-capacity feature. INT8 codes/scales
require **43.75% fewer logical table bytes** than BF16; MXFP8 requires
**48.4375% fewer**, excluding allocation overhead. These percentages
describe PLE table storage, not total model memory.

The existing worker-local adapter bridges upstream format selection and
streaming scale loading; it does not replace the shared host
constructor. These bridges can be removed when upstream provides
equivalent PLE quantization-selection and scale-loading extension
points.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. With `--quantization ascend`, the PLE format is inferred from
`quant_model_description.json`. No new flag or environment variable is
introduced.

| Mode | Existing configuration | Constraints |
| --- | --- | --- |
| NPU-resident INT8/MXFP8 | `--engram-config
'{"cpu_offload":false,"dp_shared_memory":false}'` | Selected-row
dequantization |
| Registered-host INT8/MXFP8 | `--engram-config
'{"cpu_offload":true,"dp_shared_memory":false}'` | BF16 activations,
ETP=TP; synchronous lookup with NPU graph replay |

INT8 is validated on A3 and A5; MXFP8 requires A5/950DT. Asynchronous
pinned-host prefetch is unsupported. Optional local-DP sharing retains
the existing `dp_shared_memory:true` interface; its multi-DP hardware
validation is pending.

### How was this patch tested?

**Operator correctness and integration**

| Validation | Result |
| --- | --- |
| A3 NPU operator and BF16 host regressions | **22 passed, 5 MXFP8 cases
skipped** |
| A5 NPU operator and BF16 host regressions | **27 passed** |
| Dequantization reference | Exact BF16 comparison (`rtol=0`, `atol=0`;
matching NaNs for E8M0 special encodings) |
| Exported-checkpoint layer checks | Sampled INT8/MXFP8 code/scale rows,
streaming loading, eager lookup and changing-ID graph replay match the
BF16 reference |

Coverage includes production chunk boundaries, width 160/256, empty and
non-owned IDs, INT8 extrema, E8M0 zero/NaN encodings, INT32/INT64 sliced
IDs, graph replay, metadata rejection, scale-loading errors, distinct
code/scale pointer buffers and retryable host cleanup. CPU tests also
cover format dispatch and the upstream reduction contract.

Reproduce in a matching NPU environment:

```bash
pytest -q tests/e2e/nightly/single_node/ops/singlecard_ops/triton/test_ple_quant_lookup.py tests/e2e/nightly/single_node/ops/singlecard_ops/triton/test_ple_host_lookup.py
```

**Model accuracy**

| Hardware | Quantized model | Original BF16 model | Difference |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| A3 | 91.4% | 91.7% | -0.3 percentage points |
| A5 | 91.4% | 91.7% | -0.3 percentage points |

These GPQA Diamond results were supplied by the author from separate
evaluations. They are model-accuracy evidence, not a new evaluation of
this final PR head or an isolated measurement of host placement.
Complete per-run evaluation settings and raw records are not attached
here.

**Operator performance**

Compare compact storage with the same code/scale values expanded to
BF16, using identical IDs and full registered host tables of width 160:
40,000,192 rows per rank for A3/TP8 and 80,000,384 for A5/TP4. Tables
contain synthetic values at production dimensions. Both paths run in the
same process and require exact BF16 agreement before timing.

| Hardware / format | IDs / distribution | Quantized (us) | BF16 (us) |
Latency reduction |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| A3 INT8 | 4096 / TP8-uniform | 25.002 | 35.363 | 29.30% |
| A3 INT8 | 65536 / TP8-uniform | 320.183 | 459.063 | 30.25% |
| A5 MXFP8 | 4096 / TP4-uniform | 41.700 | 41.541 | -0.38% |
| A5 MXFP8 | 65536 / TP4-uniform | 614.551 | 685.004 | 10.29% |
| A5 MXFP8 | 131072 / TP4-uniform | 1263.867 | 1401.373 | 9.81% |

Measurements use CANN 9.2.1 r89, torch 2.10.0, torch_npu 2.10.0.post7
and triton-ascend 3.6.0.post2. Values are median NPU-event latency per
lookup in fixed-ID steady-state graph replay: A3 50 calls/graph and 9
samples; A5 100 calls/graph and 15 samples with alternating measurement
order. Both use five graph replays for priming. The operator document
includes small shapes and fully owned results: some small shapes
regress, including A5 128/256 IDs by 20.68%/11.07%. No all-shape speedup
is claimed.

These are operator measurements, excluding model computation, TP
reduction, network and cold-cache behavior. The 131072-ID row is an
additional operator shape; it is not one full service prefill.

Benchmark entry point: `benchmarks/benchmark_ple_lookup.py`; production
dimensions, reference, sampling method and commands are documented in
`vllm_ascend/ops/triton/docs/ple_lookup_quantized.md`.

**A5 end-to-end performance (128K input / 1K output)**

Compare `shared_awq` (compact MXFP8 PLE) with `bf16_reference` (the same
PLE code/scale values expanded to BF16) on Qwen3.8-Flash-Next W4A8-MXFP
with shared AWQ. All other model weights and serving settings are held
constant. This isolates the PLE storage/lookup choice; the reference is
not the original full-BF16 model.

| Concurrent requests | Quantized PLE output throughput (tokens/s) |
BF16 PLE output throughput (tokens/s) | Throughput increase | Quantized
/ BF16 TTFT (s) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 58.73 | 56.57 | +3.82% | 10.20 / 10.29 |
| 8 | 89.92 | 87.23 | +3.09% | 46.78 / 47.49 |

Each request contains exactly 131072 input tokens and generates 1024
output tokens with `temperature=0`, `seed=20261118` and
`ignore_eos=true`. Each concurrency has two warmup batches followed by
three measured batches; all requests in these reported batches
succeeded. Values are medians across the three measured batches. Output
throughput is total generated tokens divided by client-observed batch
elapsed time, including prefill and decode. TTFT is the median of each
batch's per-request time to first non-empty streamed text.

Settings: A5/950DT, TP4/DP1 with expert parallelism, registered-host PLE
(`cpu_offload=true`, `dp_shared_memory=false`), context limit 141312,
prefill chunk 4096, prefix caching and async scheduling enabled,
`FULL_DECODE_ONLY` NPU graphs, and MTP with three speculative tokens.
The run uses the CANN 9.2.1 r89 software stack listed above, the
r89-compatible serving adapter with PR21730, and the final PR lookup
operator. It does not establish full latest-main framework validation.
These paired results show a modest throughput benefit for the two
measured workloads; they do not imply a speedup for every workload.

**JIT specialization**

`EMBEDDING_WIDTH`, `CHUNK_ROWS`, `GROUP_SIZE`, `BLOCK_SIZE` and
`IS_MXFP8` specialize addressing, vector shape and format decoding.
`shard_start`/`shard_end` use `do_not_specialize`; ID count changes the
launch grid. Dtype, alignment class, compile-time values, scalar types,
compiler options and target changes can still require variants. No
autotuning, custom warmup registry or global runtime cache is
introduced.

Fresh-cache operator checks record one compiler entry per kernel during
priming and no additional entries for the tested dynamic shapes and
graph replays. Model-worker tracing separately records **one
quantized-kernel compiler entry per worker at startup and zero
additional serving entries**: A3 8 workers/16 observed ID shapes per
worker in a partial run; A5 4 workers/42 shapes across 205 completed
128K/1K requests. IDs are INT64 with stride `(16, 1)`;
width/group/block/chunk are 160/32/256/4194304. Compiler entries can
include persistent-cache resolution; source/module renames can
invalidate cached artifacts. This serving validation uses the
r89-compatible adapter plus the tested operator; it does not establish a
complete latest-main framework installation.

**Validation scope**

Operator correctness, matched A5 model performance, benchmark and
specialization evidence are provided above. The file/parameter naming
refactor preserves the kernel and wrapper AST after reversing identifier
renames and inlining the exact constants; CPU PLE regression tests pass
(56 tests, using the CI-pinned upstream PLE module and its NVFP4 helper
with the r89 framework). Hardware measurements describe the tested
computation before this refactor; hardware validation of the refactored
source remains subject to CI. A complete latest-main serving validation,
optional multi-DP hardware coverage and required CI/CODEOWNERS approvals
remain merge checks. Current-head CI is authoritative.

[Feature][Model] Integrate CANN LightningIndexerV2 via its Torch interface for QSA (#21771)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Replace Qwen3.8/Qwen4Exp QSA's per-query LightningIndexer V1 path with
request-batched LightningIndexerV2 through the CANN-provided
`cann_ops_transformer` Torch interface.

- Keep one adapter in `models/qwen4_exp/lightning_indexer.py`, calling
CANN Torch operators directly with existing QSA tensors. Clamp query
boundaries to the supplied rows and generate the schedule from the same
bounds; zero-length dummy requests and invalid logical positions handle
padding. No extra live-count fields or indexer-builder replacement.
- Preserve request-level lengths and page tables, avoiding per-query
expansion/page-table gathers and zero-padding query heads. Preserve QSA
output packing and buffer reuse.
- Remove the unused V1 selector, redundant wrapper and obsolete tests.
Delegate operator parameter validation to CANN. No csrc, MTP or
model-tutorial changes; #21851 is not a required dependency.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

QSA requires the CANN-provided `cann_ops_transformer` extension and
matching CANN libraries exposing Liv2 and its metadata operator. No new
CLI flags.

### Performance evidence

Historical A3 comparison (2026-11-13): full 48-layer model, eight-card
PD, MTP3, D graph mode; 128K input / 1K output, concurrency 128,
configured 100% prefix cache, through the proxy. Both variants completed
512/512 requests; each captured approximately 2.2 seconds of profiling.

| Metric | LI V1 | Torch Liv2 | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Main indexer kernel, weighted mean | 311.52 us | 136.31 us | **56.25%
lower latency** |
| Output throughput | 3133.19 token/s | 3005.87 token/s | -4.06% |
| MTP acceptance | 85.75% | 73.51% | -12.24 percentage points |

Kernel means use 16 matched rank/query-row/page-geometry groups and V1
call-count weights; they exclude metadata/input preparation and output
packing. The ABIs differ, including V1 head padding. This single-run
release-stack comparison predates the latest cleanup and demonstrates a
kernel-level benefit, **not an end-to-end speedup**. Acceptance/output
differences remain unattributed.

### How was this patch tested?

- **Current padding refactor (`d3b088684`):** 4 focused CPU adapter
tests, Ruff, and changed-file mypy checks for Python 3.10/3.11/3.12
passed. On A3, the matching runtime source passed 23 initial NPU
boundary checks plus 14 padding/graph-replay checks (including NaN dummy
queries and changing live batches), and 14 four-layer MTP3 PD proxy
requests. Full local `format.sh ci` was attempted but blocked during
actionlint environment installation; full CI is not claimed.
- **A3/A5 reduced-model integration:** adapter `5e0f372b` passed 7/7
proxy requests on each platform, including long input and concurrency 4.
A3 used eager mode; A5 completed D main-model and MTP graph capture.
Existing runtimes required separate compatibility patches, excluded from
this PR; these are functional checks, not full-model accuracy results.
- **Earlier full-model integration** with #21851 (`abd0dcf`) and
separate MTP compatibility changes: 21 NPU operator tests passed; GPQA
Diamond 10-case sample scored 10/10 with model-default sampling. An
earlier greedy run scored 9/10 with one repetition/truncation case still
unresolved.

Exact standalone-head full-model validation and repeatable end-to-end
performance/accuracy parity remain unverified.

[Feature][MoE] Add exact expert offload for V2 eager and decode ACL graphs (#18604)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

This PR adds exact MoE expert offload for single-device inference on
Ascend 950PR/950DT (A5). It enables large MoE checkpoints, including
`DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731` and `GLM-5.3-Flash`, to run when their full
expert weights exceed NPU memory capacity.

Prepared target routed-expert weights and scales are stored in pinned
host memory. Router-selected experts are loaded into stable per-layer
NPU slots without changing routing, dropping experts, or substituting
expert weights. Prefill, mixed batches, and decode capacity overflow use
a reusable full-expert pool.

- Support Model Runner V2 (MRV2) eager execution and `FULL_DECODE_ONLY`
ACL graphs, including expert transfers during graph replay and
transfer-failure handling.
- Support both synchronous and asynchronous scheduling. Offload
execution and weight publication remain serialized per worker.
- Reuse native checkpoint loading and quantization post-processing,
preserving the prepared NPU weight and scale layouts.
- Support checkpoint-native DeepSeek V4 DSpark and GLM-5.3-Flash MTP
with eager drafting and fixed verification. Only target routed experts
are offloaded; draft experts remain fully resident on the NPU and follow
the native loading and execution paths.
- Keep offload boundary tests in `tests/ut/distributed/expert_transfer/`
and provide two focused A5 E2E cases in
`tests/e2e/pull_request/one_card/test_expert_offload_a5.py`, registered
in the existing A5 suite and routed to `a5-4`.

### Does this PR introduce any user-facing change?

Yes. Expert offload is disabled by default. Enable it through Ascend
additional configuration:

```bash
--additional-config '{"expert_offload_config":{"enabled":true,"num_device_experts":68}}'
```

[BugFix] Preserve draft LM-head TP for DFlash2 and DSpark (#22074)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

DFlash2 fails at construction when
`finegrained_tp_config.lmhead_tensor_parallel_size > 1`. Its candidate
selector bypasses the ordinary draft-logits hook, so enabling the flag
alone does not align the different requests owned by DP ranks. Qwen3/K3
DSpark has a related QuaRot loading issue: rebuilding the draft LM head
with an empty prefix silently loses fine-grained sharding, leaving a
full-vocabulary copy when ordinary TP=1.

This change:
- Pads and gathers each DP rank's hidden-state rows before evaluating
vocabulary shards, then routes shard-local TopK candidates back to their
request owners with all-to-all. Full-vocabulary logits are not
exchanged.
- Preserves score/ID precision, vocabulary-padding masks, and
empty/uneven DP batches.
- Preserves fine-grained LM-head TP when rebuilding unrotated DFlash2
and Qwen3/K3 DSpark weights for a QuaRot target. Rebuilt draft LM heads
use ordinary TP when fine-grained LM-head TP is disabled, including with
PCP enabled. Draft-owned heads and the no-QuaRot sharing path are
preserved.
- Enables DFlash2's support flag while keeping LiLiCorr unsupported.

Related: #19478 proposes broader dynamic-capacity changes. This PR
retains current static capacity and addresses DFlash2's
candidate-specific request routing and QuaRot weight reconstruction on
current main.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. DFlash2 can start and serve with fine-grained LM-head TP, for
example:

```json
{"finegrained_tp_config": {"lmhead_tensor_parallel_size": 8}}
```

The draft embedding is unchanged. Existing sampling and parallelism
restrictions remain. Documentation and release note
`release_notes/fragments/22074.yaml` are included.

### How was this patch tested?

**Unit tests:** on upstream main `efd21a1e6` plus this patch, with vLLM
`4ba787ec9` (0.33.0):

```bash
python -m pytest -q \
  tests/ut/spec_decode/test_dflash_pcp.py \
  tests/ut/spec_decode/test_dflash2_v2.py \
  tests/ut/spec_decode/test_dflash_model_loading.py \
  tests/ut/worker/v2/test_lmhead_tp_utils.py \
  tests/ut/model_executor/test_qwen3_dspark.py
```

Result: **264 passed**, 17 dependency/deprecation warnings. Added cases
compare per-request candidates with a full-vocabulary reference across
eight shards, including idle/uneven ranks, vocabulary padding,
FP16/BF16/FP32/FP64, token IDs beyond exact FP32 range, and output
scaling/softcapping. QuaRot tests verify the reconstructed LM-head
prefix; existing capacity and unsupported-path tests are retained.

**CI regression follow-up (`abe3713fd`):** updated the remaining QuaRot
layer-construction test stub to accept and verify `prefix`, and
corrected the production-speculator assertions to require DFlash2
support while retaining LiLiCorr's opt-out. This addresses the
regression-test review feedback.

In an isolated CPU container, the two affected suites on `6465d7558`
reproduced **23 failed, 51 passed**. After the test-only fix, the
expanded suite passed **338 tests** (14 dependency/deprecation

```bash
TORCH_DEVICE_BACKEND_AUTOLOAD=0 python -m pytest -q \
  tests/ut/spec_decode/test_dspark_model_loading.py \
  tests/ut/worker/test_model_runner_v2_finegrained_tp.py \
  tests/ut/spec_decode/test_dflash_pcp.py \
  tests/ut/spec_decode/test_dflash2_v2.py \
  tests/ut/spec_decode/test_dflash_model_loading.py \
  tests/ut/worker/v2/test_lmhead_tp_utils.py \
  tests/ut/model_executor/test_qwen3_dspark.py
```

above plus `tests/ut/ops/test_vocab_parallel_embedding.py` passed **412

**QuaRot refactor integration and CI regression (`cc7df7816`):** merged

[Feature][Engram] Add local host VMM for shared A3 tables (#21623)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

On A3 with DeepSeek-V4.1 Flash, TP1/DP16 and shared CPU-offloaded
Engram, registering the second table's scales can fail with
`aclrtHostRegisterV2` error 207001. Correlated device logs show
`remap_pfn_range` returning `-ENOMEM`; the exhausted device-side
resource is not established.

Automatically use node-local Host VMM for eligible A3 shared Engram
tables. Each layer has one physical allocation containing codes and FP32
scales; rank 0 publishes checkpoint rows, and local ranks import their
own mappings. Before selecting VMM, each rank loads the native library
once in the collective constructor, and all ranks test allocation,
export, import and mapping with a 1 GiB-aligned probe. Library and
allocation errors are gathered through the same group protocol. If
probing or table allocation fails, all ranks switch to HostRegister only
after coordinated cleanup succeeds; a cleanup or collective failure
aborts instead. This keeps the existing lookup kernel and does not
remove device mappings.

The allocation uses generic HOST placement because the available
device/PCI topology did not provide a verified device-to-NUMA mapping.
It does not claim NUMA-local placement or the performance of the
previous allocator.

### Does this PR introduce any user-facing change?

Yes. On A3, an INT8 shared CPU-offloaded table automatically uses Host
VMM when the runtime VMM probe succeeds on all ranks. No new
configuration is required:

```bash
--engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true,"dp_shared_memory":true}'
```

Existing `shared_engram` configurations keep their own backend. Dummy
loading and unsupported layouts keep their existing paths. The current
PR does not modify Mooncake; P/D integration and shutdown have not been
validated on the current head. The build must include the Host VMM
library and use a compatible CANN/driver stack, with a shared `/dev/shm`
namespace for local ranks. The native library and Python wrapper use ABI
version 3 and must be built together. Stop admission and drain requests
before shutdown; recovery after a lost peer or unfinished remote
transfer is not validated.

### Relationship to existing work

The native allocator and host-buffer wrapper reuse the implementation in
#21245. #16689 is a related host-backed Engram backend that currently
rejects `cpu_offload`; #19528 explores a separate MemFabric/GVA path.
This PR targets the existing shared CPU-offload path and its TP1/DP16
registration failure. The group protocol follows upstream [vLLM
#62359](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62359), while CANN
allocation and lifetime handling remain platform-specific.

### How was this patch tested?
Tested on A3 2P1D and 3P1D topo. Accuray passed, perf results: 
- Before: TP1 Engram OOM; 
- After: TP1 launch ok and perf:

### What this PR does / why we need it?

For decode-only batches, every query token attends to all its cached
keys, so causal masking is implicit. The FIA paths still passed the

- Chunked-prefill split: decode sub-call
- Graph capture: `full_graph_fia` (replay inherits captured params)

[BugFix] Fix merge conflict labeler concurrency group so PRs do not cancel each other (#22305)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

The PR-side debounce added to the merge conflict labeler in #22264 keyed
the
concurrency group on `github.event.pull_request.head_ref`. For
`pull_request_target` runs that expression evaluated empty, so every run
fell
back to the shared `refs/heads/main` group. Result: all PRs share one
group and
each new `synchronize` event cancels the previous queued run, even on
unrelated
PRs.

Evidence from 2026-11-18 (after the debounce merged at 06:10):

- Every cancelled labeler run carries the annotation
`Canceling since a higher priority waiting request for Merge Conflict
Labeler-pull_request_target-refs/heads/main exists`
regardless of the PR's branch (checked runs for #22216 and several other
PRs).
- 09:19–09:26 UTC shows a chain of cancellations across different PR
branches,
  each cancelled roughly a minute after creation by the next PR's run.
Example: PR #22216's run at 09:19:24 (e7e90762) was cancelled by a
different
  PR's run at 09:20:31.

Fix: key the group on `github.event.pull_request.number`, the documented
key
for PR-scoped concurrency groups, so only runs of the same PR debounce
each
other. The push-event fallback (`github.ref`) is unchanged.

Until this merges, the labeler is effectively single-slot repo-wide: all
PR
runs except the newest get cancelled before picking up a runner.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No. CI-only change; the merge-conflict label behavior is unchanged, it
just runs
correctly per PR again.

### How was this patch tested?

- YAML syntax validated locally; full lint via CI pre-commit.
- Behavior cannot be verified locally (concurrency is a GitHub-side
effect):
after merge, watch the next labeler runs — same-PR synchronize should
cancel
the previous run of that PR only, and the annotation group should
contain the
  PR branch scope instead of `refs/heads/main`.
- CI testing only; no hardware involved.

[Refactor][KV Pool] Refactor layerwise KV pooling into data-plane strategies (#21314)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Isolate the plane-specific logic of the layerwise AscendStore KV pool
behind an explicit data-plane interface, deduplicate the idioms both
backend protocols had re-implemented, and delete two generations of
unreachable legacy transfer paths. Net: 21 files, +1255/−1698. No
behavior change is intended: the block-key session protocols and the GVA
protocol bodies were moved verbatim (verified by normalized diff against
the pre-move code), wire-key string formats are unchanged (byte-for-byte
assertions in tests), and the full UT pass/fail set is identical to the
upstream/main baseline — checked after every commit of the original
series, and re-verified at the rebased head against the new baseline.

Note: this series was rebased onto current main after #21949 (DS4.1
shared KV reusing the GVA layerwise path) landed. The rebase keeps that
commit's worker-side additions intact on the worker and carries its
load-lease improvements (per-step lease dedup, and pinned-GVA refresh on
every occurrence of a repeated key) into the moved plane code with the
same `self.` → `worker.` rebinds, so the plane owns upstream's current
lease semantics.

## Why this refactor

Before this series, the layerwise worker carried both backend protocols
inline behind `use_block_key_layerwise` / `use_layerwise_transfer`
flags, which had three costs:

- **Protocol detail leaked into every step method.** Mooncake's session
handling (put/get sessions, revocation, retry release) and memcache's
GVA target preparation (batch_alloc, read leases, partial-key
repointing) shared method bodies, so every transfer-path function had to
reason about which protocol it was currently in. The Mooncake session
functions were module-level helpers with no interface shape at all.
- **Safety-relevant reasoning was duplicated.** The contiguous-hit scan,
the fail-open existence-probe policy, partial-key construction, and
pool-hit/save-start clamping each existed in plane-specific copies that
could drift — and a drift in any of them is a correctness bug, not a
style issue.
- **Dead protocol paths.** Two generations of unreachable entries were
still present: the Key-layer transfer threads, and the older
generator-era `retrieve_layer`/`store_layer` entries with their
`get_event` signal. They imply a third transfer protocol that can never
run.

## Design: a two-hook data plane

`LayerwiseDataPlane` (new `layerwise/planes/`) is a step-level interface
with exactly two hooks, because those are the only two points where the
protocols must diverge at step granularity:

```
store_masks → prepare_sessions → save loop → _build_shared_save_data
            → load loop → _build_shared_load_data
            finish_sessions at load completion / abort
```

- **`prepare_sessions`**: each plane opens its pool sessions and/or
resolves transfer targets here, holding its own ordering invariants. For
the GVA plane the load-before-save order is a protocol invariant — load
preparation queries the GVA registered by the *previous* step's
snapshot, so it must complete before save allocation repoints the
partial key at a fresh one — so it lives (documented) inside the plane
instead of the shared timeline. The fold is behavior-neutral: save-loop
planning is a pure function of pre-step request state and reads no
GVA-pair output, the pair reads no planning output, and the one crossing
(allocation failure setting `can_save = False`) converges to the same
empty save set in both orders.
`test_layerwise_load_is_prepared_before_next_save_allocation` locks the
internal `["load", "save"]` order unchanged.
- **`finish_sessions`**: releases the step's pool-side load sessions.
The GVA plane is a no-op because GVA loads read through worker-held
addresses — the only remaining no-op, and it is the *behavior*
difference, not interface noise.

Earlier revisions of this series exposed three (originally four) hooks;
folding the GVA window into `prepare_sessions` removed the last no-op
stub and the last protocol-specific concept from the interface, so the
upper layer no longer sees GVA vs block-key at step level.

The worker keeps the genuinely shared machinery (key construction, store
I/O batching, session tracking, failure recording, the save-disable
circuit breaker) and drives the timeline through the interface; planes
resolve worker helpers at call time instead of caching bound methods, so
a helper swap keeps affecting the whole step. Backends declare their
plane as a class attribute (`memcache: "gva"`, `mooncake: "block_key"`)
and a factory binds it at config time.

## Detailed changes

- **`layerwise/planes/` (new)**: `BlockKeyDataPlane` owns both block-key
session protocols (single-group and hybrid multi-group, moved verbatim);
`GvaDataPlane` owns the GVA protocol (save-side GVA allocation,
load-side lease/GVA resolution, moved verbatim from the worker).
`backend/mooncake_layerwise.py` shrinks to the wire-key and
layout-identity helpers — those stay in `backend/` because the scheduler
consumes them too.
- **Fold the GVA hooks into the plane** (was `prepare_load_gvas` +
`alloc_save_gvas` as two worker-driven timeline calls, then one
`prepare_gvas` hook; now inside `prepare_sessions`): the pair was always
a single window with a fixed internal order; keeping it on the timeline
exposed a GVA-specific concept through the interface and left a no-op on
the block-key side. The method bodies moved with them into
`planes/gva.py` (verbatim; shared machinery is still reached through
`self._worker`), so the GVA protocol now lives where its name says.
- **Rename `_scan_contiguous_group_hits` →
`_query_contiguous_group_hits`**: it probes the backend per block and
returns one contiguous hit run per participating group; the verb now
matches the `_query_layerwise_block_hits` helper it drives.
- **Share `LoadSpec.pool_hit_tokens` / `LoadSpec.clamp_save_start`**:
identical token-resolution and clamping reasoning existed in both planes
and the worker.
- **Unified existence probes** (`_probe_pool_missing_keys`,
`_filter_pool_existing_keys`): the fail-open policy is deliberate (an
unreadable pool costs hits; a bogus skip costs the blocks themselves),
so it is defined once and cannot drift.
- **`LayerwiseKeyBuilder` owns partial-key construction** (dead
`make_hit_check_keys` shims dropped): the key format is wire protocol
and needs a single point of truth.
- **Delete unreachable legacy paths**: the Key-layer threads
(`KVCacheStoreKeyLayerSendingThread` / `RecvingThread` + their test
class) — `LayerwiseKVPoolWorker` is only constructed with
`use_layerwise`, where the scheduler rejects any data plane other than
`block_key` / `gva` at startup, and the non-layerwise deployment uses
`KVPoolWorker`, which never had them; the generator-era `retrieve_layer`
/ `store_layer`, their payload type `LayerMultiBlockReqMeta` and the
`get_event` shadow signal — the only waiter was `retrieve_layer` itself,
while the current protocol synchronizes on per-layer
`layer_load_finished_events`, so the recving thread kept setting a
signal nobody waited on; `_async_load_enabled` (constant `False`, no
callers, no base-class slot).
- **Drop one-line forwarders**:
`_finish_current_layerwise_load_sessions` (the hybrid rollback path even
bounced plane → worker → plane) and `_make_mooncake_layerwise_key` (a
group-0 forwarder; the hybrid path already called
`_make_layerwise_full_key` directly, so all block-key sites now use one
spelling). Pure indirection hides the real call target.
- **Drop the recving thread's dead failure-policy knob**:
`raise_on_transfer_failure` was declared and stored on the recv side but
never read — load failures already carry their own per-block /
per-request semantics (invalid-block marking, failed-request reporting,
the load abort event). The sending thread keeps the flag; its save path
genuinely reads it.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No. This is an internal refactor of the KV transfer and pooling logic:
wire-key string formats, the user-facing config knobs
(`layerwise_max_transfer_blocks`, `layerwise_max_transfer_bytes`,
`h2d_stagger_us`) and all deployment behavior are unchanged, so no
release-note fragment is added.

### How was this patch tested?

- `tests/ut/distributed/ascend_store`: the full-suite pass/fail set is
identical to the upstream/main baseline — checked after every commit of
the original series and re-verified at the rebased head (the single
passing-test delta is the test of the deleted dead dataclass).
- `test_layerwise_load_is_prepared_before_next_save_allocation` passes
explicitly, locking the GVA internal order through `process_layer_data`.
- Block-key session protocols and GVA protocol bodies moved verbatim
(normalized diff); wire-key formats unchanged (byte-for-byte test
assertions).
- Performance no-regression check with AISBench (prefix-cache workload)
on 8 Ascend 905PR cards in a PD-disaggregated deployment (prefill 4 /
decode 4, both DP=4 / TP=1): `python3 aisbench_test.py --input_len
131072 --prefix_num 16 --output_len 1024 --data_num 64 --concurrency 16
--request_rate 0 --dataset_type prefix_cache --repeat_rate 90%
--prefix_test`. Baseline runs use upstream main; candidate runs use this

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Enable experimental prefill context parallelism (PCP) for Kimi K3 and
K3.1 with RecoverSSM by providing the permutation and mask metadata
required by the KDA path.

Share the PCP capture-configuration and buffer initialization between
the ordinary Kimi KDA and RecoverSSM builders, preserving their
respective base-class initialization. Reuse the existing Kimi KDA PCP
metadata attachment logic.

Update the Kimi K3/K3.1 release fragments in response to #21549 review:
clarify the limited validation scope and remove unqualified A3/A5
hardware-matrix tags pending broader validation.

parallelism (PCP).

[CI] Align fla_npu pins on 26.10.0+feature and classify its GDN window (#21203)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

#22141 bumped `FLA_VERSION` to `26.10.0+feature` in the six Dockerfiles
but left the four workflow pins and the GDN window registry on `26.9.1`,
so every CPU unit-test run on top of main fails in the guard added by
#21936:

```
FAILED tests/ut/ops/test_gdn_window_guard.py::test_declared_pins_agree fla_npu pins disagree: ['26.10.0+feature', '26.9.1']
FAILED tests/ut/ops/test_gdn_window_guard.py::test_declared_window_is_known conflicting fla_npu pins: Dockerfile*=26.10.0+feature,
  .github/workflows/*=26.9.1
```

The second failure is the same root cause: `_declared_window()` returns
the `UNKNOWN` sentinel when the pins disagree, hence the `assert <object
object at ...> is not <object object at ...>` line.

This PR completes the bump:

- Workflows now install
`flash-linear-attention-npu-*===26.10.0+feature`:
`_selected_tests.yaml`, `_selected_tests_upstream.yaml`,
`schedule_e2e_upstream_test.yaml`, `schedule_main2main.yaml`. CI
therefore
  exercises the same wheel the images ship, instead of 26.9.1.
- `KNOWN_OPP_WINDOWS` gains `"26.10.0+feature": 8`.
- `dependency_version_management.md` follows the new pin, and the
main2main example is corrected to the mirror pin the workflow actually
uses (the old dev-wheel download snippet no longer matched any file).

The v26.10.0-feature wheel still contains the fixed-window AscendC
kernel, so no dispatch change is needed: `recurrent_gated_delta_rule`
has no `arch22`/`arch35` OPP directory and its header declares `MAX_MTP
= 8` (verified in the published a2 wheel). The `8`-token cap, the
`spec_state_indices_tensor.shape[1] > _MAX_RECURRENT_GDN_TOKENS` gate,
and the A2 `gdn_fixed_spec_recurrent_fallback_min_query_len=9`
workaround all stay.

involves
boundary conditions (e.g. empty input, single/zero element, min/max

I

### What this PR does / why we need it?

This PR enables adaptive verification with LM head Tensor Parallelism

adaptive estimator reads logits, making the combination safe at

adaptive-verification compatibility and its
confidence-head/full-decode-graph requirements.
- Adds regression test coverage for DSpark LM-head TP construction
validation and model-level draft-logit padding/trimming with adaptive
verification enabled.

DeepSeek-V4-Flash across seven validation configurations covering
LM-head TP and adaptive verification, plus the pre-change startup error
check.

[CI][Misc] Update FLA_VERSION to 26.10.0+feature in Dockerfiles (#22141)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

This PR updates the `flash-linear-attention-npu` package used by the A2,
A3 and
A5 images from `26.9.1` to `26.10.0+feature`:

- `Dockerfile` / `Dockerfile.openEuler` (A2)
- `Dockerfile.a3` / `Dockerfile.a3.openEuler` (A3)
- `Dockerfile.a5` / `Dockerfile.a5.openEuler` (A5)

The version comes from the `v26.10.0-feature` release of

[flashserve/flash-linear-attention-npu](https://github.com/flashserve/flash-linear-attention-npu/releases/tag/v26.10.0-feature).
Note that the release tag contains `-feature`, while the wheel version
is
`26.10.0+feature`; the Dockerfiles use the wheel version.

This release contains the KDA forward update that raises the per-pack
sub-sequence limit from 1024 after the underlying `aclIntArray` limit
was
lifted.

No Dockerfile architecture branching is added. The wheels are published
on the
Ascend mirror for both host architectures, and `pip` selects the
matching one:

| Package | x86_64 | aarch64 |
|---|---|---|
| `flash-linear-attention-npu-a2` | yes | yes |
| `flash-linear-attention-npu-a3` | yes | yes |
| `flash-linear-attention-npu-a5` | yes | yes |

The wheel requires glibc >= 2.34 and `GLIBCXX_3.4.29`, which is
satisfied by the
Ubuntu 22.04 / openEuler 24.03 base images used here.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. Users of newly built A2/A3/A5 images get the FLA NPU
`26.10.0+feature`
kernels. No API or configuration change is required.

A release note fragment `release_notes/fragments/<PR number>.yaml`
should be
added with category `dependency` once the PR number is known.

### How was this patch tested?

- Verified that the Ascend mirror publishes the `26.10.0+feature` wheels
for
  A2, A3 and A5 on both `x86_64` and `aarch64`.
- Verified the changed Dockerfiles only bump `FLA_VERSION`; no install
logic or
  architecture detection is modified.
- `git diff --check` passes.

A full image build was not run locally because it requires the Ascend
CANN base
image and NPU build environment. The change is covered by the existing
image
build CI once triggered.

```text
Recipes / Validate
    └── Ascend configuration / Validate
```

remain visible.** Source and zero-coverage failures always block.

[BugFix][Scheduler] Preserve Mamba checkpoints in consumer chunked prefill (#21575)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

#### Overview

- **Branch:** `hechengkai:fix/mamba-consumer-prefill-checkpoints` →
`vllm-project:main`; an independent checkpoint fix discovered during
#21574 validation, after #20835 was merged.
- **Problem:** a KV consumer with a computed prefix bypasses Mamba/KDA
alignment even during ordinary chunked prefill, omitting a reusable
state checkpoint.
- **Reproduction:** recorded main `6d4f1c0`; prompt 2305, common cache
granularity 1152, expected reusable prefix `floor((2305 - 1) / 1152) *
1152 = 2304`. The budget limits each scheduling iteration, not cache
granularity.

| Prefill budget | External hit / expected | Consumer / no-pool
checkpoint boundary | Max absolute raw-logit error vs no-pool |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2048 | 1152 / 2304 | 1152 / 2304 | Cold: **1.03125** |
| 1024 | 2304 / 2304 | 2048 / 2304 | Reload: **8.4921875** |

- **Table interpretation:** requests reached token 2305, but missed
checkpoint 2304. A full external hit alone does not prove correct state
restoration; the 2048 case also diverged before reload.

- **Upstream contract:** Merged vLLM
[#51113](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51113) fixes
Mamba/GDN align-mode prefix-cache poisoning under EAGLE/MTP: a chunk-end
`state@364` could be published as `state@1600`. It extends prefill
alignment beyond `last_cache_position`, realigns mid-block resumes, and
retains `last_cache_position` as a mandatory snapshot stop. In
`mamba_cache_mode="align"`, the pinned [prefill
splitter](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/24420b7a341af37a9bc3186e6fc6062512e0aa58/vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py#L606-L660)
and [regression
tests](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/24420b7a341af37a9bc3186e6fc6062512e0aa58/tests/v1/core/test_mamba_align_chunk_split.py#L270-L319)
require cached states to match their advertised token boundaries. GLM
KDA uses this Mamba cache interface, so ordinary consumer prefills must
retain the required checkpoint stops.

#### Minimal change

- Keep the consumer/positive-prefix gate. Compute the remaining request
tokens from the request-computed, newly matched local, and external
prefix counts; ordinary prefill, including single-module MTP, continues
through checkpoint alignment.
- Preserve the complete window only when `num_new_tokens >
remaining_tokens` within the consumer/positive-prefix gate
(verifier/async placeholders), matching upstream
`_mamba_block_aligned_split` handling. Remove the method-name `is_mtp`
bypass.
- Reuse the existing alignment path: budget2048 changes chunks `[1152,
1153]` to `[1152, 1152, 1]`. No changes to lookahead reservation, cache
publication, backend keys, worker or kernels.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. KV consumers retain reusable Mamba/KDA checkpoints during ordinary
chunked prefill, including single-module MTP, while verifier/async
windows remain protected. A bugfix release-note fragment is included.

[Performance] Reuse head-first QKV storage in GDN prefill to eliminate redundant copies (#22010)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Supersedes #21739 and targets `main`.

The GDN prefill convolution can expose Q, K and V as sequence-first `[B,
T, H, D]` views of contiguous head-first `[B, H, T, D]` storage. The
base adaptor currently copies each tensor into sequence-first order,
then copies each back into head-first order for ChunkGDN. This round
trip costs six layout copies.

The adaptor converts each input to a head-first view and packs it only
if needed. Dense head-first inputs reuse their storage. A token slice
with gaps is packed directly in the layout ChunkGDN consumes. Q and K
are normalized over the same final dimension `D`.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Eligible prefill inputs automatically skip the six copies on the base
device adaptor. No configuration change is required.

### How was this patch tested?

The seven CPU-tensor layout tests were rerun on this port to `main`
(base `a1df499e0762`). The A3 hardware, serving and GPQA results below
were collected for the release-branch patch in #21739.

On A3, a 2,048-token prefill slice (17 leading tokens removed, 8 Q/K
heads, 24 V heads, head dimension 128, BF16) produced
elementwise-identical outputs and final recurrent states against the
previous PR head (`a04482cce`). Across 24 profiled calls per version,
the mean summed Q/K/V copy-kernel time fell from **110.04 to 24.46 µs**:
three AsStrided plus three Transpose kernels became three Slice kernels.
This measures layout copies for one sliced invocation.

A full AISBench GPQA Diamond rerun on the #21636 W4A8 integration stack
with the updated prefill function scored **179/198 (90.40%)**. The
previous layout implementation on that stack scored 183/198 (92.42%).
All 198 requests succeeded; two answers could not be extracted. This
single unseeded sampling run (32-way concurrency, 140,000-token output
cap) missed the 90.71% reference threshold by one correct answer. The
earlier three-run release-branch comparison below used a 120,000-token
cap.

#### Operator and serial-request performance

On Ascend A3 (W8A8, TP8, DP1), a rank-0 trace of a 16,435-token prefill
showed **6 → 0 QKV copy kernels in each of 180 GDN windows** across 36
layers, eliminating **20.37 ms of summed copy-kernel time** on that
rank. With profiling disabled, median TTFT for serial requests of the
same length fell from **2,278.90 to 2,245.56 ms (−1.46%)**, with 20
requests per variant.

#### Serving performance

We ran each workload once per variant on Ascend A3 with W4A8 weights,
using the same inputs and target request rate. A is the original
implementation and B enables the optimization. The table covers all
measured requests. Throughput and completed QPS changes are relative to
A.

| Input / output tokens | Requests per variant | Target req/s | Mean
TTFT, A → B (s) | Mean TPOT, A → B (ms/token) | Input / output
throughput change | Completed QPS change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 16K / 1 | 840 | 1.00 | 2.102 → 2.137 (+1.70%) | — | −0.02% / −0.02% |
−0.02% |
| 128K / 1 | 192 | 0.16 | 15.609 → 11.953 (−23.42%) | — | +0.63% /
+0.63% | +0.63% |
| End-to-end 16K / 1K | 660 | 1.00 | 2.205 → 2.240 (+1.61%) | 16.59 →
16.78 | +0.31% / +0.31% | +0.31% |
| End-to-end 128K / 1K, 90% shared prefix | 400 | 1.23 | 10.667 → 6.469
(−39.35%) | 16.63 → 16.55 | +1.65% / +1.65% | +1.65% |

Mean TTFT increased slightly in both 16K workloads. Shorter queues
accounted for most of the TTFT reduction at 128K. In the end-to-end 128K
/ 1K run, both variants had an **88.83% prefix-cache hit rate**. Mean
queue time on the prefill service fell from **6.482 to 2.336 s**, while
mean prefill execution time fell from **2.961 to 2.923 s**. Neither
end-to-end workload produced an AISBench steady-state window.

#### Numerical correctness and GPQA Diamond

All seven layout tests passed with CPU tensors (`python -m pytest -q -p
vllm_ascend.ops tests/ut/ops/test_gdn_layout.py`). In 11 numerical
comparisons on Ascend A3, Q, K, V, the GDN output and the final state
matched elementwise. Coverage included sequence lengths of 51, 63, 64,
65 and 4,096 tokens, non-contiguous token slices and continued state.
The hardware checks used release commit `62fe4cde69d9` with the layout
patch applied for variant B.

We evaluated Qwen3.8-Flash-Next W4A8 with AISBench through the
prefill/decode proxy. Only the prefill implementation changed. Each
variant answered the same 198 GPQA Diamond questions in three zero-shot
chain-of-thought runs, with B evaluated first. Both used
`temperature=1.0`, `top_p=0.95`, `top_k=20`, concurrency 32 and a
maximum output length of 120,000 tokens. No request-level sampling seed
was set.

| Run | A · original | B · optimized | B − A (percentage points) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 183/198 (92.42%) | 177/198 (89.39%) | −3.03 |
| 2 | 181/198 (91.41%) | 181/198 (91.41%) | 0.00 |
| 3 | 180/198 (90.91%) | 181/198 (91.41%) | +0.51 |
| **Mean accuracy** | **91.58%** | **90.74%** | **−0.84** |

B produced five fewer correct answers across the three runs. The per-run
differences varied in direction under stochastic decoding, so these
results alone cannot attribute the lower mean accuracy to the layout
change.

---

#### Testing

- [x] **Boundary / edge-case coverage**: I reviewed whether this change
involves
boundary conditions (e.g. empty input, single/zero element, min/max
values,
off-by-one, sequence-length limits, integer overflow). Where applicable,
I
added unit tests covering these edge cases in `tests/ut/` or
`tests/e2e/`.
- [x] **Regression test**: If this PR fixes a bug, I added a regression
test
  that would fail without the fix.
- [ ] **Error / failure path coverage**: I covered abnormal paths
(exceptions,
timeouts, out-of-range, division by zero) in addition to the happy path.
- [x] **Meaningful & reliable tests**: New tests assert real behavior
and are
  not written merely to satisfy CI.
- [ ] **Performance impact**: If this PR touches a performance-sensitive
path,
  I attached benchmark results and added performance regression tests.

commits.message:
[CI][BugFix] Move review-event gate retrigger to a standalone workflow_run relay (#22221)

## What this PR does / why we need it?

Two real-PR failures exposed two independent holes in the ci-gate
review-retrigger design (`refresh_ci_gate.py`, #22106/#22133):

**1. Shadow skipped check allowed a merge through the gate (PR
#22202).**
`pr_test.yaml` previously triggered on both `pull_request` and
`pull_request_review`. A review-triggered E2E run skips `ci-gate` (its
`if` requires `pull_request`), but GitHub still creates a check-run for
the skipped job. Two check-runs then share the required `ci-gate`
context name on the head SHA, GitHub judges the required check by the
latest one, and a skipped check counts as satisfied — so the PR became
mergeable in the window before the real gate rewrote its verdict. #22202
merged (by its author) exactly through that window: merge at 14:28, gate
rewrite at 14:39.

**Fix:** move the retrigger out of `pr_test.yaml` entirely. The
`pull_request_review` trigger is deleted (with a comment forbidding its
return), and a standalone `pr_refresh_ci_gate.yaml` carries it. The
required `ci-gate` check now has exactly one producer, so a shadow
skipped verdict cannot exist.

**2. Fork-PR rescue failed with HTTP 403 (PR #22134).**
`GITHUB_TOKEN` is read-only for *every* workflow run tied to a fork PR,
regardless of the triggering event, and fork runs see no repository
secrets either — so `refresh_ci_gate.py`'s `rerun-failed-jobs` POST
always 403s for fork PRs, and the late-owner-approval rescue silently
degraded to a manual-rerun comment. This is the "fork PR actions:write"
risk item flagged as unverified when the retrigger landed; it is now
verified to fail.

**Fix:** split the retrigger into a two-hop relay:
- `pr_refresh_ci_gate.yaml` (`pull_request_review`, read-only token is
enough) only packages the review payload as an artifact;
- new `bot_ci_gate_refresh.yaml` (`workflow_run`, base repo context with
a writable token — the same safe pattern as the existing comment bot: it
never checks out or executes PR code, the script comes from the default
branch) downloads the payload and performs the actual re-run.

Also in this PR:
- `bot_ci_gate_comment.yaml` listens to the new `CI Gate Refresh`
workflow so the retrigger's own-failure comment contract still reaches
the PR;
- `pr_refresh_ci_gate.yaml` cancels a prior in-flight refresh per PR
(`cancel-in-progress: true`): with several reviews in quick succession,
the latest review wins; a cancelled relay loses nothing because the
script re-judges with live review state;
- `refresh_ci_gate.py`: no logic change, docstring only.

## Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No user-facing behavior changes for the happy paths (same-repo PRs
behave as before). Two observable changes:
- Fork PRs: a late owner approval now *actually* rescues the gate
(previously it 403'd and required a manual rerun, #22134).
- Review-event runs no longer produce a second, skipped `E2E / ci-gate`
check on the PR (the #22202 merge-bypass vector).

## How was this patch tested?

- `refresh_ci_gate.py` logic is unchanged: its 28 unit tests pass
unchanged (`pytest .github/workflows/scripts/test_refresh_ci_gate.py
--noconftest`).
- All touched workflow YAMLs parse cleanly (`yaml.safe_load`).
- `bash format.sh ci`: all hooks pass except the local gitleaks scan,
which fails for known local-environment reasons (no secrets in the diff;
CI will confirm).
- CI testing only for hardware/e2e aspects — no NPU behavior is touched.
- End-to-end behavior depends on `workflow_run` reading workflows from
the default branch, so it cannot be verified before merge. Post-merge
verification points:
1. fork PR + late owner approval → gate flips green automatically (the
#22134 scenario);
  2. same-repo PR rescue path unchanged;
  3. veto (CHANGES_REQUESTED / dismissed) still re-arms the gate red;
4. a review no longer creates a second, skipped `ci-gate` check on the
PR.

[Test][GDN] Guard the recurrent verify window against fla_npu pin bumps (#21936)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

`#16292` protected the legacy AscendC recurrent GDN kernel by adding a
local
per-sequence cap and a width gate in `vllm_ascend/ops/gdn.py`:

```python
_MAX_RECURRENT_GDN_TOKENS = 8
use_upstream_recurrent = ... or (
    spec_state_indices_tensor.ndim == 2 and spec_state_indices_tensor.shape[1] > _MAX_RECURRENT_GDN_TOKENS
)
```

That number describes the *installed fla_npu OPP*, not this repository.
Since
fla_npu `#1070` the arch22/arch35 kernel consumes a sequence in windows
and has
no per-sequence cap, but nothing connects the Python constant to the
kernel
that is actually installed. Two silent failures follow from a version
bump:

* bump fla_npu and leave the code alone → `k >= 8` keeps going to the
strided
  Triton kernel forever, with no error and no gain from the new kernel;
* delete the cap before the wheel ships it (or delete only half of it) →
a
  9-token window reaches the single-window kernel, which returns without
  writing output: the request produces garbage instead of an error.

This PR adds a CPU-only tripwire that reads the operator that is
installed and
fails when the code and the kernel disagree, naming the exact edit:

* classify the OPP from what the wheel installs: an `arch22/`/`arch35/`
directory means the window-loop kernel (no cap); otherwise the root
header's
`MAX_MTP = N` is the legacy fixed window. Vendors are visited in the
order
`opp/vendors/config.ini` declares, so an overlaid tree cannot describe
the
kernel that does not run. An unrecognised tree **fails** instead of
skipping,
  so a layout change cannot silently disable the guard.
* when `fla_npu` is not installed (e.g. a local environment), fall back
to the
version this repository pins, and require that version to be classified
in
  `KNOWN_OPP_WINDOWS` first.
* check the definition **and** its use site: with the window-loop kernel
both
`_MAX_RECURRENT_GDN_TOKENS` and the `spec_state_indices_tensor.shape[1]
> ...`
comparison must be gone (inlining `8` is caught); with the legacy kernel
the
constant must equal the header's `MAX_MTP` and the comparison must
reference
  it (deleting only the comparison is caught).
* the A2 `gdn_fixed_spec_recurrent_fallback_min_query_len = 9`
workaround is
tied to the same generation, since it was measured on the kernel that
the V2
  OPP replaced.

No production code changes. The existing cap stays until the fla_npu
release
containing `#1070` is pinned; at that point the test prints the removal
steps
and the follow-up patch applies them.

Reference: `#16292`, `#64427`.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No. This PR only adds a unit test, plus one allowlisted word in
`typos.toml`
(the OPP vendor directory is literally named `tbe`); the released
artifact
behaves identically. Per `release_notes/README.md`, no release-note
fragment is
added because a user of the wheel or image cannot observe a difference.

### How was this patch tested?

CPU only, no device, no `fla_npu` import (`tests/ut/conftest.py`
replaces the
package with a stub, so the test locates the real distribution through
`importlib.metadata`).

Thirteen tests: three repository-state checks (pins agree and both kinds
of
file are seen, the pin is classified, the code matches the installed
kernel),
one scanner check (`==` and `===` are both recognised), eight detector
tests
(legacy 8, legacy 16, `arch22`, `arch35`, unknown layout, vendor order,
`config.ini` priority order, and the width comparison in its three
shapes) and
one self-check for an unclassified repository state.

Six combinations were exercised with the OPP swapped in place, against
the
current `main` sources (`vllm_ascend/ops/gdn.py` `1e6a9916`,
`vllm_ascend/device/hardware_profile.py` `4cc9a895`) and the
`flash-linear-attention-npu-a3==26.9.1` wheel that the CPU CI job
installs:

| OPP | code | result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 26.9.1 (legacy) | unpatched | 13 passed |
| 26.9.1 (legacy) | cap removed (follow-up patch) | 1 failed — asks to
restore the cap |
| V2 (fla_npu main `5830fa6`) | cap removed | 13 passed |
| V2 | unpatched | 1 failed — asks to remove the cap |
| V2 | constant removed, `shape[1] > 8` inlined | 1 failed — reports the
inline comparison |
| 26.9.1 (legacy) | comparison removed, constant kept | 1 failed — asks
to restore the cap |

The follow-up patch was also checked against current `main` (`git apply
--check`): it still applies, with offsets only.

### Why not fix this in fla_npu?

`#1070` is already merged and fixes the kernel on `main`. The remaining
risk is
the hand-off in this repository (pin bump vs. code change), which only
this
repository can enforce. A capability API on the fla_npu side was
proposed but
is not being pursued.

### Notes

* The guard verifies routing, not numerics: it cannot prove that a
9-token
window produces correct output, only that it is no longer routed away
from
  the kernel or into a kernel that cannot handle it.
* Wide verify windows on `arch35` (A5) are not covered by on-device
tests yet;
  the guard would accept them as soon as the V2 wheel is pinned.

---

### Checklist

#### Testing

- [x] **Boundary / edge-case coverage**: the guard pins the 8/9-token
boundary
  on both kernel generations — `MAX_MTP = 8` in the installed header vs.
`shape[1] > 8` in the dispatch — and the detector tests cover the legacy
8-token and 16-token headers, the `arch22`/`arch35` layouts, an unknown
  layout and vendor ordering.
- [x] **Regression test**: both silent failures a version bump can
produce are
covered — the kernel upgraded while the cap stays behind, and the cap
removed
while the legacy kernel is still installed (including the half-edit that
  deletes only the comparison or only the constant).
- [x] **Error / failure path coverage**: an unrecognised OPP tree fails
instead
of skipping, and the pin fallback fails when the pinned version is not
listed
  in `KNOWN_OPP_WINDOWS`.
- [x] **Meaningful & reliable tests**: the tests read the OPP that is
actually
installed (or the pins declared in this repository) instead of mocking a
  layout, and were exercised against six real code/OPP combinations.
- [ ] **Performance impact**: not applicable — a CPU-only unit test that
touches
  no performance-sensitive path.

[Attention][Feature] Support TP × PCP KDA sharding for GLM-5.3-Flash (#21510)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

This PR enables joint Tensor Parallelism (TP) and Prefill Context
Parallelism (PCP) head sharding for the KDA layer in GLM-5.3-Flash.
Previously, PCP participated in KDA head sharding only when TP was 1.
Projections, convolution weights, and recurrent state are now sharded
across TP × PCP ranks in TP-major order, matching Mooncake V2 state
transfer. The output projection combines PCP contributions before the
optional TP reduction so the sequence-parallel decoder can still defer
TP reduction.

RecoverSSM now accepts TP > 1 with PCP > 1 on KV producers. Its records
use the same local head count as the projections and recurrent state.
PCP consumers and colocated PCP execution remain unsupported; the
speculative-decoding, PP=1, DCP=1, cache-mode, and stochastic-rounding
checks remain in place.

Follows the KDA sharding approach in #21017.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. Native KDA and RecoverSSM prefill producers support joint TP × PCP
head sharding. The KDA head count must be divisible by TP × PCP. The
RecoverSSM documentation and release note describe the supported
configuration.

### How was this patch tested?

**2026-11-17 conflict/CPU-UT update (`ec722e555`):**

- The two failed CPU jobs in run
[43708732339](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/actions/runs/43708732339)
stopped during `git rebase`, before pytest. Rebased the feature onto
main `915d58873`, resolved the KDA/input-projection-TP conflicts, and
preserved the RecoverSSM and PCP reduce-scatter changes previously
carried by merge commits. Repeating the CI rebase command succeeds.
- Explicit `tp_group` projections retain their own shard rank/size and
collectives; default projections compose TP x PCP. Added
weight-loader/collective regression coverage with nontrivial default TP
and PCP groups; retained main's input-projection and static-bias
coverage.
- Linux CPU-only container, no NPU devices, real pytest with the
repository CPU mocks: **385 passed** on each of vLLM verified main
`ba15685ab7f4f5fbed8630bbb7441f8837e76fbe` and `v0.33.0`. Tested
`test_glm5next_kda_{pcp,dispatch,reduce_scatter,input_projection_tp,contracts,state_dtype}.py`
and `test_glm5next_recoverssm_config.py` under `tests/ut/models/`.
- Ruff check/format, Markdown lint, codespell, typos, forbidden-import,
boolean-context-manager, long-function and diff-whitespace checks
passed. `bash format.sh ci` was attempted on Windows but stalled
installing the actionlint Go environment; the complete check remains
covered by [CI run
44009645674](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/actions/runs/44009645674).
- No new NPU benchmark was run for this conflict repair. The original
native-KDA hardware results below remain evidence for `28666d61d`, not a
benchmark of the rebased head; RecoverSSM multi-card hardware validation
remains pending.

Validated on A3 with MRV2 and GLM-5.3-Flash W8A8C8 using PD separation
on one host: eight logical NPU devices for Prefill **TP2/PCP4** and
eight for Decode **TP8/PCP1/DCP1**. Prefill uses eager mode; Decode uses
`FULL_DECODE_ONLY`. `enable_pcp_o_proj_weight_sharding=true` in both
arms.

Baseline: main `faa43c37d` **plus a GLM KDA/Mamba state-transfer fix**
that infers head shards and PCP replicas from cache shapes and copies
the corresponding head slices for this PD topology. Candidate: this PR
at `28666d61d`, without that local baseline patch. Both use vLLM
`24420b7a34`.

Completed three rounds of all **198 GPQA Diamond questions per version**
on 2026-11-16, with `max_tokens=65536`, `reasoning_effort=low`,
temperature 1, top_p 0.95, seed 1024 and client concurrency 100. Each
branch reuses one service startup for its three rounds, with five smoke
requests and a 100-request concurrency probe before measurement;
requests are drained and prefix caches reset between rounds. Decode
graph replay and actual concurrency 100 were verified for both services.
Mean results across all three rounds:

Candidate change |

Both versions have higher TTFT in their first round. Across rounds 2-3
